record.paper_title: Euclidean random matrices: solved and open problems
record.context_brief: Practical supersymmetric formalism for Euclidean random matrices
record.original_question: For the Euclidean random-matrix setting attached to stationary points of a Hamiltonian H[x], where one studies the matrix M[x] at z = 0 and the measure built from exp(-βH[x]) together with determinant-based weights, can one construct a practical analytical formalism in which the BRST-type supersymmetry of the problem is not merely present formally but is used as a central working tool for computing the properties of the model?

evidence.quote: In the framework of Euclidean random theory there are two questions that are quite relevant and may be the most interesting for Euclidean Random theory: • How to construct and to use in a practical way a formalism where the supersymmetry of the problem plays a crucial role?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H[\mathbf{x}]$ be a Hamiltonian for $N$ particles with positions $\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\dots,x_N)\in\mathbb{R}^{dN}$, and let $M[\mathbf{x}]$ denote the Hessian matrix of $H$ (or, more generally, a Euclidean random matrix whose entries depend on the particle positions, considered at spectral parameter $z=0$). Consider the constrained measure on configurations $\mathbf{x}$ that are stationary points of $H$, given (formally) by
$$d\mu(\mathbf{x}) \;\propto\; e^{-\beta H[\mathbf{x}]}\,\bigl|\det M[\mathbf{x}]\bigr|\,\prod_i \delta\!\bigl(\partial H/\partial x_i\bigr)\,d\mathbf{x},$$
with the determinant weight encoding the Jacobian of the stationarity constraint. It is known that this measure carries a hidden BRST-type supersymmetry (a fermionic nilpotent symmetry exchanging the bosonic constraint fields with auxiliary Grassmann ghosts) which relates the bosonic and fermionic sectors of the associated supersymmetric representation.

Construct an explicit, practical analytical formalism for computing physical observables of $M[\mathbf{x}]$ (such as its averaged resolvent, density of states, and correlation functions) in which this BRST supersymmetry is not only formally present but is used as a central, active computational tool: e.g., as the organizing principle for Ward identities, for the choice of order parameters, for closure of self-consistent equations, and for non-perturbative resummations beyond the standard cavity, replica, or perturbative supersymmetric expansions.
artifact.category_tag: Euclidean random matrices and BRST supersymmetry
artifact.status_search_result: The question of building a practical analytical formalism for Euclidean random matrices that elevates the BRST/supersymmetry of stationary-point measures to a central computational tool is posed as one of the most relevant open directions for the field. While supersymmetric methods in random matrix theory and BRST treatments of constrained measures are well developed individually, no general practical formalism specifically exploiting this supersymmetry for Euclidean random matrices appears in the literature; recent works mention only "hidden supersymmetric properties" used in particular cases. Status appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean random matrices: solved and open problems - ADS
status_evidence.snippet: Lists construction and practical use of a formalism where supersymmetry plays a crucial role among the most relevant open questions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly identified as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: The Supersymmetric Method in Random Matrix Theory and Applications to QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews the supersymmetric method in RMT but does not develop a BRST-centered framework for Euclidean random matrices at stationary points.
status_evidence.claim: Existing supersymmetric RMT formalisms do not address the specific question.

status_evidence.title: Supersymmetry in Random Matrix Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys supersymmetric techniques in RMT without providing the practical BRST-based working tool requested for Euclidean random matrices.
status_evidence.claim: No practical BRST-centered formalism for Euclidean random matrices is reported.
